# Vendored Packages

This directory contains source-vendored copies of the Cordis framework and its foundation libraries. They are copied into this monorepo instead of being depended on via npm, so that the harness fully owns its framework layer (auditable, patchable, pinned).

All vendored packages use the **`@deepseek-ai` scope** (`cordis` → `@deepseek-ai/cordis`, `@cordisjs/plugin-<x>` → `@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-<x>`). The manifest table records upstream versions and source commits; each package manifest carries its Harness release version and publication metadata. References to vendored packages use `workspace:~`, so local builds resolve the workspace packages and published ranges permit patch updates within the same minor version. Upstream MIT `LICENSE` files are preserved in each package directory.

This file covers the manifest, the local-modification log, and the procedure for **updating** an existing vendored package. To **add a new** one, see the cookbook guide: [docs/cookbook/adding-a-vendored-package.md](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-vendored-package.md).

Intentionally **not** vendored (verified unused by this set): `reggol`, `@cordisjs/utils`, `@cordisjs/unyaml` (dev-time YAML import hook only).

## Local modifications

Keep this log exhaustive — every divergence from upstream must be listed. Each entry has a stable ID: remove an entry when its divergence no longer exists, and never renumber or reuse IDs. The next new entry is V119.

- **V1 · `hmr/src/index.ts`**: removed the `./locales/en-US.yml` / `./locales/zh-CN.yml` imports, the `.i18n({...})` call on the `Config` schema, and the `src/locales/` directory. Rationale: those imports require a runtime YAML loader hook (`@cordisjs/unyaml`) that we do not vendor; the i18n texts only localize config descriptions.
- **V2 · All `package.json` files**: regenerated for Harness releases with scoped names, release versions, publication metadata, precise bundled-runtime and `lib/types/**/*.d.ts` / `.d.ts.map` file entries, source exports where applicable, and declaration metadata pointing at `lib/types`. References within the vendored set use `workspace:~`. HMR declares `esbuild` as a direct dev dependency for its imported `BuildFailure` type, Loader requires `node-addon-require-builtin@^0.1.4` to match published app runtimes, and Include declares `yaml@^2.9.0` instead of upstream's `^2.9.1` so the workspace installs one copy of `yaml`.
- **V3 · All `tsconfig.json` files**: regenerated to extend the repo-root `tsconfig.base.json`, emit TypeScript intermediates to `lib/types`, and declare project references.
- **V4 · Vendored TypeScript source internal specifiers**: changed local relative imports/exports from upstream's specifier shape to explicit `.ts` specifiers so TypeScript rewrites emitted JS to `.js` while declarations keep explicit, NodeNext-safe `.ts` specifiers. This includes `loader/src/config/isolate.ts` using `declare module './entry.ts'`. Core's upstream source already uses explicit `.ts` specifiers. Type-only dependencies use `import type` or inline `type` modifiers so ESM output does not retain erased interfaces.
- **V5 · `schemastery/tsdown.config.ts`, `logger-console/tsdown.config.ts`, `fetch-file/tsdown.config.ts`, `loader/tsdown.config.ts` and `plugin-im-core/tsdown.config.ts`**: ours, not upstream files — per-package build-shape overrides (dual ESM+CJS output; separate node/browser entries; Loader's single self-contained entry; and `plugin-im-core`'s two entries, the runtime `lib/index.js` and the `lib/testing.js` testkit behind its `./testing` subpath) for the repo-root tsdown build. They read the JS emitted under `lib/types` and then write the publish runtime entries under `lib/`. Like the regenerated tsconfigs, they are not part of the upstream sync surface.
- **V6 · `cordis/src/fiber.ts` lifecycle hardening**: locally closes three reentrant disposal gaps. An effect's owner-list wrapper is registered before its setup body runs, so an unload begun from inside setup awaits setup and every collected cleanup; synchronous setup failure removes the wrapper and rolls back collected cleanup. Async cleanup stays owner-visible until quiescence, and Cordis's internal effect composition joins an already-running cleanup while repeated public disposer calls retain their upstream single-shot result. Effect creation is rejected while the owner is `UNLOADING` (while `PENDING` and `LOADING` remain legal), preventing cleanup-time registrations from escaping the unload snapshot. Child fibers register and receive their parent-owned disposer before `internal/plugin` publication, resolve dependency declarations added by that notification before activation, drain effects attached while pending, and contain teardown-notification failures per observer so one callback cannot starve peers or interrupt ownership cleanup.
- **V7 · JSDoc enrichment**: added `@param`/`@returns` tags and contract documentation (disposal semantics, waterfall veto, bail conditions, error cases) across the public plugin-author surface — `Context` (class, statics, the `isolate()` rule that isolated scopes never fall back to an injected view, and the `Context` interface properties incl. `[Context.root]`), module re-exports, shared utility helpers, `EventsService`, `Fiber`, `ValidationError` and its path helpers, `RegistryService`, `ReflectService`, `Service` and its intercept-metadata members, `LoggerService` and their `declare module './context.ts'` overloads. The upstream line comment on `reflect.ts`'s exported `locate()` is rewritten as JSDoc. Loader documentation covers `loader/src/{index,internal,config/entry,config/group,config/isolate,config/tree,config/utils}.ts`, including entry ownership, tree mutation methods, the `!!js` discriminator, entry option validation, source positions and `ModuleNotFoundError`. The upstream `EventsService.dispatch()` deprecation annotation is omitted: DSH enumerates callbacks to contain each observer failure independently, which the typed dispatch methods do not provide. Timer retains its local class and helper summaries; its README is local documentation because the upstream package has none. Cosmokit and Schemastery add summaries to their exported helpers, types and namespaces, logger-console to its exporters and config namespace, and HMR to its build-failure logger in `hmr/src/error.ts`. Comment-only; no code changes. Motivation: the website API-reference generator renders these docs and hard-errors on undocumented members. Retire this entry when the enrichment is upstreamed.
- **V9 · `hmr/src/index.ts` module-watcher readiness and native paths**: realpath the existing watch base, classify framework modules and attach listeners before reporting readiness, and compare config paths using both canonical and configured spellings. This preserves Node module-cache identity across Windows short-name paths and filesystem aliases. The main watcher uses `ignoreInitial: true` so startup reads do not trigger another refresh; exact profile patch watching is owned by `packages/boot/hmr/src/watch-config.ts`. The Include change listener logs a rejected `Include.refresh()` instead of leaving the rejection unhandled; the rejection reports unsaved runtime changes while Include keeps its running tree. Covered by `packages/boot/hmr/tests/watch-config.spec.ts` and `scripts/cordis-vendor-hmr-include.spec.ts`.
- **V10 · Vendored Node-compatible TypeScript**: marked erased imports explicitly across `cordis`, `loader`, `include`, `hmr`, and `schemastery` so Node's native TypeScript transform does not request types as runtime exports. Schemastery's source uses an ESM default export and its package declares `type: module`. Conditional exports select `.mjs` for import and `.cjs` for require; without them, concurrent imports under module-hook hosts reach the CJS entry and can race its require of ESM Cosmokit (`ERR_REQUIRE_ESM_RACE_CONDITION`).
- **V11 · Include patch and YAML exports**: `include/src/index.ts` exports upstream `applyPatches` as `applyEntryPatches` with its `PatchResult` type, so `dsh --dump-config` composes entries with the same algorithm that mounting uses. It also exports `parseEntryYaml`, `stringifyEntryYaml` and `entryYamlErrorPosition` over the `!!js` YAML dialect, using the `yaml` options with which `_read()` parses Include's own file, so every DSH reader and writer of Include-dialect YAML uses Include's parser. `parseEntryYaml` throws the first parse error or warning, such as an unknown tag or an alias without a preceding anchor (V30), adds line positions to alias errors so `entryYamlErrorPosition` reads them, and returns `undefined` for an empty document; `stringifyEntryYaml` always writes with `aliasDuplicateObjects: false`, matching the previous `noRefs` output, and offers no option to emit aliases, while Include's own writer keeps upstream's options. Covered by `packages/boot/app-boot/tests/config-reload.spec.ts`, `scripts/cordis-entry-commit.spec.ts` and `scripts/cordis-entry-yaml.spec.ts`.
- **V14 · Include persistence results**: `include/src/index.ts` keeps an error for unsaved journal changes. `flush()` retries pending writes and rejects while changes remain unsaved; `stop()` returns the same result and always stops the child tree; a later successful flush clears previous errors. A failed `refresh()` can also reject while runtime changes remain unsaved. Patch-owned changes route to the parent Include, so callers that need them persisted must flush that parent too. The constructor omits upstream's `ctx.hmr.watch(this.filename, () => this.refresh())` registration because neither HMR provider exposes `watch()`; both find each Include by scanning loader entries for its `filename` and call `refresh()`. Ordinary Fiber teardown keeps its error containment. Covered by `scripts/cordis-include-journal.spec.ts` and `packages/host/directory-picker-auto/tests/loader-composition.spec.ts`.
- **V15 · Configuration access across Core, Loader, Include and HMR**: rc.11 Core owns raw `Fiber.config`, `internal/config(fiber, next)`, `internal/commit` and awaited `internal/update(config, next)`. Root-fiber candidate resolution remains available without a plugin schema. Local `rawConfig`, `resolveConfig(candidate)` and `effectiveConfig` accessors retain the DSH consumer API. Fiber caches the object passed to activation or a successful update that keeps the instance; candidate resolution is pure, failed or superseded updates cannot replace the cache, and volatile updates retain references. Loader resolves only entry roots and excludes Group/Include tree carriers, so nested `!!js` expressions wait for their own injections. Include retains its tree-carrier marker and public patch exports, and HMR transfers raw config through the accessors. Covered by `scripts/cordis-config-access.spec.ts`, `scripts/cordis-core-lifecycle.spec.ts` and the boot/HMR suites.
- **V16 · `cordis/package.json` publishes `src`**: added `src` to the `files` list, joining the other eight vendored packages. Cordis declares `"./src/*": "./src/*"` in its exports, so a tarball without `src` publishes an export map pointing at absent files; the release change judgement also reads `files` to decide whether a diff reaches the payload, and a package whose only published paths are build output has no tracked path to match.
- **V17 · `@deepseek-ai` rescope**: every vendored manifest `name`, every internal dependency entry among the vendored set, and every module specifier that reaches them use the scoped names in the manifest table's `npm name` column. Directory names, version numbers, and dependency ranges are unchanged, and no upstream runtime identifier is renamed — `Symbol.for('schemastery')` and Schemastery's `vendor:` metadata field keep their upstream values. Re-apply with `pnpm run rescope-vendor --apply` after a sync; the table's two name columns are the mapping, restated for consumers in [docs/rescope.md](../docs/rescope.md).
- **V22 · Volatile config across `cosmokit`, `schemastery`, `cordis`, and `loader`**: Cosmokit supplies immutable references and framework-owned commits; `deepEqual` treats two references as equal, propagates strict comparison into arrays, compares every array slot with holes treated as undefined, handles cycles conservatively, compares URLs by normalized href, and compares other opaque objects by identity in strict mode. Schemastery adds `.volatile()`, optional/default inference, placement validation without eager lazy-schema expansion (a lazy inner is validated once when built), metadata-free serialized node compatibility, serialized metadata, reference-aware simplification, unsupported volatile values reported as `ValidationError` with their path, and `.default()` accepting the raw input type `Partial<S>` because a volatile field makes the output type carry references. Loader's save path calls `simplify` with its schema receiver (`unparse.call`), an independent fix for the unbound-`this` call. Cordis exports consumer types without changing Fiber lifecycle. Loader compares raw options strictly in `Entry.update`; for a config-only change on an active fiber it calls the pure `equalExceptVolatile` function in `config/diff.ts`, which narrows the Standard Schema to Schemastery's `Schema` type (a new type-only `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` dependency of `loader`) and recursively skips fixed volatile paths using schema metadata without executing config hooks or validation. Missing or null object nodes compare using their declared defaults, including nodes without volatile descendants; schema backedges retain raw comparison. Entry passes its actual schema and preserves ordinary context and custom-update lifecycles. For a volatile-only change, `Entry._commitVolatile` takes the canonical fiber `entry.fiber.ctx.fiber` (`Entry.fiber` holds the registry wrapper), re-parses the raw config through `Fiber.resolveConfig()`, compares ordinary effective values, commits references and emits the instance-local `loader/volatile-update` declared in `loader/src/index.ts`; a changed ordinary effective value falls back to the ordinary remount, and an invalid candidate is logged while the raw config stays retained for the next activation. Cosmokit provides reference enumeration and commits, and `simplify` is called with its schema receiver. The package READMEs document these additions; schema tests live in `scripts/volatile-config.spec.ts`, Loader runtime and real-file tests in `scripts/loader-volatile-update.spec.ts`, and code replacement tests in the HMR module suite.
- **V23 · `loader/src/config/entry.ts` module identity**: retains each entry's raw import result as `moduleNamespace`, before plugin export normalization. HMR matches that object to Node's cached module namespace and updates it after a successful reload. `EntryTree.import()` keeps its existing arguments and return value; `loader/README.md` documents the additive field.
- **V24 · `timer/locale/{en,zh}.json` display metadata**: local English and Chinese titles and descriptions for the Settings plugin inventory. `timer/package.json` exports and publishes these locale resources.
- **V25 · Loader lifecycle adaptations**: before a combined context/config update, Loader refreshes dependencies locally, which prevents activation against stale isolation bindings; disabled-entry updates await disposal. Failed fibers require an explicit update after correcting their input or dependencies. Core retains the effect hardening in V6; rc.11 owns dependency teardown ordering and superseded-activation handling.
- **V26 · `loader/src/config/tree.ts` cross-tree moves**: backports [cordiverse/cordis#271](https://github.com/cordiverse/cordis/pull/271), merged after `v4.0.0-rc.12`. When `EntryTree.update()` moves an entry into a group of another tree, the entry and the same-tree members of its group move their store registrations to the target tree, and the move is rejected before either tree changes when the target tree already holds one of their ids. The source tree receives a removal and the target tree a creation, without `legacy` or `from`. Upstream at `v4.0.0-rc.12` keeps the entry registered in the source tree and the target receives an update with `legacy`, so the Include journal writes a partial row and reconciling the target file creates a second Entry. Retire this entry when the vendored Loader includes the upstream fix. Covered by `scripts/cordis-include-journal.spec.ts`.
- **V27 · `loader/src/config/utils.ts` explicit ids with `:`**: `validateOptions()` accepts ids containing `EntryTree.sep`, so `EntryTree.create()`, `EntryTree.update()` and group reconciliation admit them; upstream rejects them with an `id must not contain` issue. `validateOptions()` keeps its upstream `sep` parameter. Generated bundles from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-creation-recommendations` prefix their row ids with `<package name>:`, and installed profiles already contain such rows. `resolve()` still splits ids on `:`, so these entries cannot be addressed by nested path. Covered by `scripts/cordis-entry-commit.spec.ts`, `scripts/cordis-loader-rc9.spec.ts` and `packages/extensions/creation-recommendations/tests/loader-composition.spec.ts`.
- **V30 · `include/src/index.ts` unresolved aliases**: backports [cordiverse/cordis#354](https://github.com/cordiverse/cordis/pull/354) (`c9fe179ce5ac484620a387a1697409cb007d4178`), merged after `v4.0.0-rc.12`. `_read()` reports each alias without a preceding anchor as a `BAD_ALIAS` `YAMLParseError` with its position, distinguishing an unknown anchor from one written after the alias; at the tag, `document.toJS()` throws an unlocated `ReferenceError` outside `ConfigFileError`. `unresolvedAliases()` matches the upstream commit verbatim. Retire this entry when the vendored Include includes #354. Covered by `scripts/cordis-loader-rc9.spec.ts` and `scripts/cordis-entry-yaml.spec.ts`.
- **V31 · IM package set in `vendor/`**: five packages come from the Satori pin recorded in the manifest — `satori-element/`, `plugin-im-core/`, `plugin-im-adapter-lark/`, `plugin-im-adapter-qq/` and `plugin-im-markdown/` — with independently pinned `element`, `http` and `fetch-file` dependencies. Their upstream sources are replaced wholesale (V32–V35, V68), so no upstream IM source is copied verbatim: the platform routes, wire envelopes, protobuf/JSON gateway formats and the token endpoints carry over, the rendering pipeline does not. Service names, events and `satori:` URLs keep their upstream names.
- **V32 · `satori-element/` is the element vocabulary**: upstream factories and aliases, the global `JSX` declaration and the blanket re-export of `cordis-element` are replaced by a typed `ElementMap` / `VariantMap` / `Element<K>` overlay over the unchanged runtime (`vocabulary.ts`), the block/inline category and tier table (`elements.ts`), the typed `h` factory with an automatic JSX runtime (`factory.ts`), `normalize()` (root `<message>`, flow-container wrapping, envelope and content-model validation; `normalize.ts`), `variantsOf()` / `variantKey()` (`variants.ts`), and the plain projection `toText()` (`text.ts`). The markdown parser is `plugin-im-markdown`'s (V68), not this package's. Plain strings are literal text — markup is parsed only by an explicit `fromMarkdown()` call.
- **V33 · `plugin-im-core/` is the IM engine**: upstream `message.ts` (`MessageEncoder`), the `Methods`/`features`/`supports(name)` surface, the component service and the protocol dependency are gone. `protocol.ts` holds the public types (`Login`, `User`, `Status`, `Meta`, `WebSocket`, `ChatRef`, `Target`, `UserRef`, `MessageRef`, `InboundMessage`, the `ButtonEvent` augmentation). A mode renders what its registry registers — the tag plus the variants its handler declares — and adapters say nothing about a chat. `mode.ts` holds `defineMode` and the `LimitKey` table, `registry.ts`, `fallback.ts` and `transform.ts` the transform engine and the core fallback table, `degradation.ts` the priced mode score, `directives.ts` the `prefer-streamable-mode` / `prefer-expressive-mode` content directives, `resource.ts` the `ResourceRef` walk and the LRU resource cache (bounded concurrency, single upload per cache key), `stream.ts` the stream scheduler with its `patch` / `edit` / `append` drivers, `errors.ts` the platform taxonomy (`PlatformError` kinds, retry hints, `published`) and `testing.ts` with `testing/` the offline testkit (`FakeAdapter`, the shared corpus, conformance, goldens). `bot.ts` splits the public `Bot` from the implementer `Adapter`: one pipeline (`normalize` → `transform` → `prepare` → `serialize` → `sendPayload`) for every adapter, mode resolution per publication, retries, `PartialSendError`, `edit`/`delete`/`stream` over the same handle, and the awaited `satori/receive` intake gate. `session.ts` keeps the slim `Session` envelope with its `onClick` callback registry, and `internal.ts` serves the `satori:` routes plus the `/_api/:name` and `/_tmp/:id` passthroughs.
- **V34 · `plugin-im-adapter-lark/` is rewritten for the protocols above**: `config.ts` is the Schemastery schema (`platform` selects the OpenAPI host and the reported platform; `cardStreaming`, `callbacks`, `allowAtAll` and the long-connection limits), `api/client.ts` the typed REST client (message create/reply/update/patch/delete/get/list, chat get, image and file upload, resource download, reactions) over an injected transport, `api/token.ts` the tenant token with a 30-minute refresh window and a single-flight refresh, `api/events.ts` the schema-2.0 event envelopes and the `LarkReferrer` contract. `errors.ts` maps the platform code table onto `PlatformError` with the `published` verdict, and `230075` stays a `limit` so the stream scheduler resolves a refused edit by recall-and-resend. `ws.ts` is the protobuf long connection (gateway handshake, fragment reassembly, heartbeats, ACK only after intake, immediate answer for `card.action.trigger`), `bot.ts` the adapter shell, `modes/post.ts` and `modes/card.ts` the two modes with their escapers, `prepare.ts` the upload stage, `send.ts` the create/reply/edit/recall routes and `decode.ts` the inbound decoder and the chat-kind mapping.
- **V35 · `plugin-im-adapter-qq/` is ported for the protocols above**: `config.ts` is the Schemastery schema with two explicit decisions — `transport: 'ws' | 'none'` (a REST-only client never opens a gateway session) and `passive.seqBase` starting at 2, because `msg_seq` is deduplicated per `(msg_id, msg_seq)` and koishi's adapter starts at 1 — plus configurable `baseUrl` and `tokenUrl`. `token.ts` caches the app access token, refreshes at `expires_in − 60 s`, refreshes single-flight and keeps serving a still-valid token when a refresh fails. `api.ts` is the typed v2 REST client (gateway, group/C2C messages, files, recall, interaction acknowledgement, C2C `stream_messages`) with self-describing `group:<openid>` / `user:<openid>` addressing. `errors.ts` maps the platform code table, the `304…` quota family and the HTTP-status fallbacks onto `PlatformError`. `passive.ts` owns the passive-reply windows and the per-event `msg_seq` budget, and reports the replies a stream may still spend. `modes/text.ts`, `modes/markdown.ts` and `keyboard.ts` render the two `msg_type` bodies and the custom keyboard, `prepare.ts` uploads media, `send.ts` publishes with the passive bookkeeping and the dedupe retry, `stream.ts` the C2C `append` driver, `ws.ts` the JSON gateway state machine and `decode.ts` the inbound decoder plus the chat-lifecycle events. Upstream's `src/` at the pin is a different file set (`bot/`, `internal/`, `http.ts`, `message.ts`, `types.ts`, `utils.ts`, `ws.ts`), so a sync must port the upstream changes into these modules instead of copying the directory over them.
- **V36 · Retained Feishu API subset**: `plugin-im-adapter-lark/src/types/` retains the `auth.ts`, `im.ts` and `contact.ts` API families from `adapters/lark/src/types/` at the Satori pin, plus the transitive closure of shared declarations in `index.ts` that those families and the handwritten adapter sources reference, with explicit `.ts` and `type` import specifiers (V4). Package `src` publication includes these files, so the subset ships in the tarball.
- **V37 · IM dependencies and build integration**: HTTP uses the repository's `undici@8.12.4`; `fetch-file` uses `mime-types@^3.0.2` / `@types/mime-types@^3.0.1` and keeps separate node/browser runtime builds; `plugin-im-markdown` declares the markdown parser closure. The vendored manifests reference each other with `workspace:~`, and every vendored tsconfig extends the repo-root `tsconfig.base.json` and compiles under its strict settings — the upstream nullability, catch and function-variance relaxations are not carried over. HTTP serializes WebSocket headers as an entry object, and adapters send multipart bodies through the `undici` `FormData` class (V42).
- **V38 · Awaited intake in `plugin-im-core/src/{index,bot}.ts`**: the awaited `satori/receive` event and `Bot.receive()`. `dispatch()` stays synchronous; the Feishu WebSocket receiver awaits intake consumers before sending a success ACK, then publishes ordinary observer events. An intake rejection withholds the ACK without discarding the caller's durable state.
- **V39 · Connection ownership in `plugin-im-core` and the adapters**: each run owns its cancellation, retry timers, sockets, initialization, heartbeat, token refresh and event-processing promises. Stop aborts setup and connections, cancels timers, closes late sockets, clears fragments and awaits tracked work; concurrent starts retain only the latest controller. Initial retry exhaustion marks the bot offline, an established connection keeps supervised reconnects, and an initialization failure can never mark the bot online. Token refresh logs no credentials and closes the connection on failure so supervision can reauthenticate.
- **V40 · Platform wire validation and limits**: the Lark long connection validates the selected envelope and application identity, ignores unselected event families, and bounds frame bytes, fragment counts, partial messages and outstanding intake operations through configuration; fragments expire, identical duplicate segments do not advance completion, and conflicting segments are rejected. The QQ gateway validates every frame, serializes dispatches in arrival order while heartbeats stay independent, and treats a missing `HEARTBEAT_ACK` as a half-open socket. Both clients answer a platform-declared failure with a typed error carrying the platform code.
- **V41 · Lark media and reactions**: Uploads go through the image and file routes and require a platform key; a media message is sent once with a caller-owned `uuid` and an authorized reply target. `createReaction()` adds one catalogue emoji (a repeated create is harmless) and `deleteReaction()` reads the message's reactions first and deletes only the one this application owns, because the platform deletes by reaction identity rather than by emoji.
- **V42 · Multipart bodies in `http/src/index.ts`**: a `FormData` built by Node's global class is rebuilt in the `undici` package's own class before dispatch, and `encodeRequest` recognizes either class. `undici@8.12.4` is a different implementation from the fetch built into Node, so its `fetch` coerced a foreign `FormData` to a string: every multipart request went out as `[object FormData]` with `content-type: text/plain`, and Feishu answered `234001 Invalid request param` for each image or file upload. Covered by `scripts/vendor-http.spec.ts`, which drives one multipart request against a loopback server.
- **V43 · Mode selection, content directives and the mode score in `plugin-im-core`**: no configuration knob and no caller picks a mode; an adapter declares its modes and their order (`Adapter.modeOrder`) and `Bot.send`/`Bot.render` resolve one per publication — every candidate mode is transformed once and the one losing the least wins, the declared order breaking a tie. Two content directives narrow the candidates: a root-level `<meta name="prefer-streamable-mode" value="true" />` keeps only modes with a stream driver (implied by `Bot.stream`, which also keeps the mode fixed for the whole stream), and `prefer-expressive-mode` keeps the broadest mode by counting the `element.*` keys it renders natively. Losing content is priced rather than counted (media, mentions and mid-message structure cost more than inline formatting, a dropped element always costs most, a folded panel costs nothing), so losing bold never weighs as much as losing a picture, and a mode can override one price or forbid a loss. `RenderResult` reports the resolved mode.
- **V44 · `<fallback>` replaced the capability layer as the way content adapts to a platform**: `@deepseek-ai/satori-element` gained the `fallback` element (each direct child is one ranked candidate, a JSX fragment counting as one) and its internal `case` node, `normalize` turns candidates into `case` children normalized as content of the element the `<fallback>` stands in, and renderers now write alternatives instead of asking what a platform supports. `RenderEngine.render` picks the first candidate whose whole subtree is native, else the last candidate with the usual lowering, records the choice in `RenderReport.fallbacks` (and charges a later candidate in `degradationScore`), so `<fallback><title>…</title><h3>…</h3></fallback>` names both the expressive and the plain spelling of one message. Nothing in the engine consults per-chat state: a mode renders what its registry registers, a declared variant included.
- **V45 · The IM capability layer is gone, not deprecated**: `plugin-im-core/src/capabilities.ts` (`ChatFacts`, `FactCache`, `LearnedFact`, `Support`, `Level`, `Capabilities`, the `element.*`/`message.*`/`limit.*` key vocabulary, `evaluateCapabilities`, `mergeCapabilities`), `Bot.supports`/`support`/`capabilities`, `Adapter.facts`, `Mode.operations`, `HandlerOptions.available`, `PlatformError.facts` and `RenderContext.caps`/`supports` were removed together with the Lark chat probe (`facts.ts`) and the QQ passive-window facts. What a platform allows is now the platform's answer at the moment of the call: a refusal rejects with the classified `PlatformError`, and content that must degrade says so with `<fallback>`. `LimitKey` moved to `mode.ts`, a mode owns its element budget in `assemble`/`check`, and `MessageStream.abort()` reports whether a recall removed the published message. The IM consumers (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-im` and its plugins) stopped querying capabilities: a renderer reads the stream strategy it was handed and writes alternatives.
- **V46 · `button[type=input]` and the Lark card mode**: the "a click sends this text as the user" button variant is `input` throughout the vocabulary (`ElementMap.button`, `VariantMap`, the core fallback, the QQ keyboard's `action.type 2` encoding). The Lark card mode does not render it: a card button can only answer with a callback, so the variant stays undeclared and the core fallback renders the label plus the text.
- **V47 · Stream diagnostics in `plugin-im-core/src/stream.ts`**: an intermediate state that cannot be rendered, a refused open and a refused tick are dropped as before — close renders again and reports — but each now logs once through the host logger inside its own `try`/`catch`, so a turn that publishes nothing says why instead of looking like a stream with nothing to say, and diagnostics never break a stream. The card mode declares the `action` variant of `<button>` under the same `callbacks` switch, which is what keeps a summary turn's stop button live.
- **V48 · `plugin-im-core/src/bot.ts` status setter reads the `bots` registry without an inject**: `set status` announced `login-updated` through `this.ctx.bots`, but `bots` is a mixin of the `satori` service, so a fiber that no longer injects that service — the teardown of a failed boot — threw `cannot get property "bots" without inject` from `Bot.offline()` and buried the real startup error. It now reads `this.ctx.get('satori')?.bots`, which answers `undefined` without the inject.
- **V49 · `plugin-im-adapter-qq/src/bot.ts` gateway host rewrite**: `gatewayUrl()` replaced the `api.sgroup.qq.com` substring of the `GET /gateway` answer with the configured REST host. In sandbox that answer is already `wss://sandbox.api.sgroup.qq.com/websocket`, and the substring occurs inside `sandbox.api.…`, so the result was `wss://sandbox.sandbox.api.sgroup.qq.com/websocket` — no DNS name answers it and every socket closed with 1006, leaving `sandbox: true` unusable. The rewrite now parses both URLs and assigns `host` only when it differs, so a host the endpoint chose for itself stays as served. Covered by `tests/bot.spec.ts`.
- **V50 · `plugin-im-adapter-qq` full-mode group messages**: a bot with 接收所有消息 switched on receives every group message as `GROUP_MESSAGE_CREATE` instead of `GROUP_AT_MESSAGE_CREATE`, so `decodeDispatch` published nothing for `@`-mentions in that group. The event now decodes through the same path, with two differences the platform dictates: the body keeps the `<@…>` mention in place, and `mentions` never carries the bot itself, so the bot's own `union_openid` — which `READY` does not report — is read once from `GET /users/@me` (`QQBot.ensureIdentity`, `QqApi.getSelf`). Only a body that mentions the bot is `mentions.self`, so background chatter stays unaddressed; a failed identity read is reported and leaves the message unaddressed rather than guessing. Covered by `tests/decode.spec.ts`.
- **V51 · `plugin-im-adapter-qq` renders code as code**: the markdown mode registered neither `code` nor `pre`, so an inline span lost its backticks and a code block arrived as an escaped paragraph — indentation and blank lines collapsed, and every `#`, `*` and `|` carried a backslash. Both tags are native now: `code` becomes a backtick span and `pre` a fenced block whose body is a new `QqNode` kind, `verbatim`, which `assemble` copies into the content without escaping, collapsing or the `\u200B` padding that keeps blank lines alive. A table the core fallback can lay out as a monospace grid follows the same path, so a narrow table reaches the chat as an aligned fenced grid — QQ markdown renders no tables of its own. Covered by `tests/markdown.spec.ts` and the mode goldens.
- **V52 · `plugin-im-adapter-qq` streaming chunk body, mode and stream identity**: `stream_messages` names a chunk's text `content_raw`, not the `content` of an ordinary send; it takes the whole state with `input_mode: 'replace'`, as its own examples do; and its first answer returns the streamed message's identity in `id` — there is no `stream_msg_id` field. The adapter sent `content`, a hand-computed suffix with `input_mode: 'append'`, and read `answer.stream_msg_id`, and none of the three mistakes shows in the status: a chunk with no text is still accepted, and a live 单聊 stream answered `remain_msg_len: 0` for a message that had just taken five characters, which turned every later append into a `shape` violation. `sendChunk` now sends the full state with `replace` and takes the stream id from the first answer's `id`, and `assertRoom` reads a zero `remain_msg_len` as "not measured" rather than as "no room", so the platform's own refusal decides. Verified against the live 单聊 stream that previously broke. Covered by `tests/stream.spec.ts`.
- **V53 · `plugin-im-core` opens a stream in the broadest streamable mode**: `Bot.stream()` resolved its mode with `preferredModeId()` — the *first* declared mode that has a driver. An adapter whose cheapest mode also streams therefore spent the whole turn in it (`text` before `markdown` on QQ), and because a streamed message fixes its `content_type` at the first chunk and can never switch, a streamed answer lost every emphasis, code block and link while the same answer sent once kept them. `streamMode()` resolves the same question the content directives ask — `prefer-streamable-mode` narrows the pool to the modes with a driver, `prefer-expressive-mode` takes the broadest of those — which needs no content, because breadth is a property of the mode registry. `preferredModeId()` remains only as the stand-in mode for a `MessageRef` this bot did not send. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-core/tests/bot.spec.ts`.
- **V54 · `plugin-im-adapter-qq` markdown mode composes a fence inside a list item or a quote**: `mapRuns` keeps a verbatim node out of the text run so nothing collapses the blank lines of a code block, which also kept it out of the prefix a list item or a block quote puts on every line it owns. A `<pre>` inside either was emitted mid-line (`- 第二项```), so the fence never opened, and the container's own marker ended up glued to the closing fence (` ```>`), swallowing every following block into that code block. `flattenRuns` flattens rendered children into lines first — text runs formatted, code lines untouched — and the two handlers prefix every line; `mapRuns` keeps its other callers. Covered by `tests/markdown.spec.ts`.
- **V55 · `plugin-im-adapter-lark` keeps code spans verbatim and leaves `= …` text alone**: card markdown escaped every `<` of user text as `&#60;`, inline code spans included, and neutralised any line that started with `=`. The platform decodes no entity inside code — a card showed `Result&#60;DsResponse, DsResponse>` — and does not consume a backslash before `=` — `= 104 B, align 8` arrived as `\= 104 B, align 8`. `cardCodeSpan` now leaves its body verbatim like `cardFence` (a span cannot open a tag, and the entity would only reach the reader), and `escapeCardBlockStart` neutralises `=` only on a line that is nothing but `=` (a setext underline), so ordinary text keeps both characters. Covered by `tests/card.spec.ts`.
- **V56 · `plugin-im-adapter-qq` markdown escaper defuses block markers instead of escaping them**: the escaper wrote `\#`, `\-` and `1\.` ahead of a line-start marker, which only works if the platform honours CommonMark backslash escapes. QQ does for `\*` but not for these: a stress answer reached the chat with `1\.` and `\#general` showing the backslash, every numbered heading of it included. Inline metacharacters keep their backslash (`* _ ~`, backtick, brackets, angle brackets); a block marker (a list item, a heading, a quote, a rule) now takes a leading U+200B instead, which is invisible and keeps the marker from being read at line start at all. Covered by `tests/markdown.spec.ts` and the refreshed corpus goldens.
- **V57 · `plugin-im-adapter-lark` names the failures behind a rejected intake frame**: the long connection logs one line per frame it could not acknowledge, and the rejection it catches is an `AggregateError` over that frame's listeners whose own message is empty — every line therefore read `… retry: AggregateError` and named no listener, leaving one intake failure indistinguishable from the next. `describeIntakeFailure` unwraps it: each aggregated failure arrives with its `name` and its `code` (`ImError` carries `persistence`, `access`, `capacity`, …), which is what says whether admission failed in intake, in a session flush or in a renderer. The ACK behaviour is unchanged and stays covered by `tests/ws.spec.ts`.
- **V58 · `plugin-im-core` settles a stream it cannot recall instead of failing the turn**: `Scheduler.resend` recalled the streamed message and, when the platform refused the delete, threw `StreamLimitError` — so the last chunk was never sent with `input_state: 10` and the chat showed that message as generating forever. QQ refuses every `DELETE` of a streamed message (`40061001`), which made this the normal outcome as soon as an answer re-parsed mid-stream: a `**bold**` that completes changes the escaped prefix of a state, so the next state cannot be appended. A stream that cannot be recalled is now closed on the state it already shows, and the final state follows as a fresh message; `limitFail` settles the same way before it throws. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-core/tests/stream.spec.ts` and the QQ adapter's `tests/stream.spec.ts`.
- **V59 · `plugin-im-core` prices a moved element**: `degradationScore` charged `degraded`, `fallbacks` and `dropped`, but an element a mode lifted out of the message body (`RenderReport.moved`) was free. A platform whose plain-text body has no image syntax therefore tied with the mode that keeps the picture inline, and the declared order decided it — so every answer mixing text with a picture was split into text, picture, text. A moved element now costs `COST_PLAIN` each, which resolves such content to the mode that can keep it: content that interleaves nothing (a picture on its own, or text alone) still ties and keeps the cheaper declared order.
- **V60 · `plugin-im-adapter-qq` embeds a picture in the markdown body**: the `img` handler published every picture as its own `msg_type: 7` message, so a mixed answer reached the chat as three messages and spent three passive replies. QQ's markdown renders `![alt #Wpx #Hpx](…)` inline — both pixel dimensions are required, `0px` meaning the source size — and fetches the source itself, so the markdown mode now keeps the picture in its own body: `assemble` leaves a placeholder and `serialize` fills it with the uploaded `qqbot-media://` reference (`prepare` uploads it for the chat, so a public URL and a local file take one path). The text mode keeps the media message, and the picture stays inside its sentence rather than taking a paragraph of its own. Covered by `tests/markdown.spec.ts` and the refreshed markdown goldens.

- **V61 · `plugin-im-adapter-lark` hands a card's pictures back as images**: a card shows its pictures by `image_key`, and the decoder turned each one into the `[image]` text reference only, so a card's picture was never a media element — `im_read_image` on such a message answered "no media element" while the card text showed nothing but a placeholder. `walkCard` now collects the keys (with a picture's alternative text as its `alt`), `interactiveNodes` emits a real `img` whose `src` is `satori:<platform>/<selfId>/images/<image_key>`, and `LarkBot` serves that route through the new `LarkApi.getImage` (`GET /im/v1/images/{image_key}`). The platform hands such a key only to the application that sent the picture: another application's card answers `234008 The app is not the resource sender`, so the card's text stays the part every reader gets. Covered by `tests/card.spec.ts`.

- **V62 · `plugin-im-core` closes a spent streaming window in place**: `Scheduler.finish` treated an elapsed `budget.until` as a reason to `resend` — recall the streamed message and publish the final state as a fresh one. What expires on the platform is *streaming* mode, not the message: the Lark driver's own `tick` already publishes a full update with `streaming_mode: false` once the 10-minute window has passed, and `close` publishes exactly that, so the card stays editable. A turn that outlived the window therefore replaced a card the reader was watching with a new message: a stopped turn's answer and its "stopped" footer arrived as a fresh bubble while the card was recalled. The window now only decides the fallback — `close` is attempted first, and a refusal from the platform still `resend`s with the same budget violation. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-core/tests/stream.spec.ts`.

- **V63 · `plugin-im-adapter-lark` edits a card message instead of streaming a CardKit entity**: `LarkBot.streamDriver('card')` answers the core `edit` driver, so a card is one `interactive` message whose card JSON is replaced with `PATCH /im/v1/messages/{message_id}`; `createCardStreamDriver`, `streamingCard`, `cardKitOps` and the entity branch of `editMessagePayload` were no longer reached from this adapter (V64 deletes them). CardKit streaming bought nothing here — a card republished whole on every state never uses incremental rendering — and cost: streaming mode closes ten minutes after it is switched on and reopens only by re-enabling it, it refuses card callbacks that update the card, and it makes the card unforwardable. Measured against the live platform: one message accepted 420 edits (120 + 300, none refused), and the only cap is 5 QPS for that message, which `CARD_STREAM_INTERVAL` (200 ms) stays under. The post mode keeps the same driver with its own 20-edit limit. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-lark/tests/{bot,card,stream}.spec.ts`.

- **V64 · `plugin-im-adapter-lark` reads the entries of a merged forward**: `LarkApi.getMessage` returned `items[0]` and dropped the rest of the answer, but `GET /im/v1/messages/{message_id}` on a `merge_forward` returns the entries after the container, each naming it in `upper_message_id` — so a forwarded conversation reached the model as the bare `[forward]` reference the event carries and nothing could ever read past it. `getMessage` now returns every item, `LarkBot.getMessage` hands them to `decodeMessage`, and `decode.ts` fills `<forward id>` with one line per entry (`sender: content`, a `br` between entries, blocks a forward cannot hold inline — a quote, a table — reduced to their text). An event still decodes the reference alone because the platform pushes no entry with it; how a nested forward and an entry's pictures are handled is V66. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-lark/tests/{decode,bot}.spec.ts`.

- **V65 · `plugin-im-adapter-lark` deletes the CardKit entity path**: `api/cardkit.ts` and `stream.ts` are gone, together with the card mode's `diff` (`CardPatch`, `CardKitOp`, `diffCards`, `diffList`, `diffComponent`, `fingerprint`), `streamingCard`, `CARD_STREAMING_CONFIG`, `maxPatchOps`, the `card-entity` part kind, the entity branch of `editMessagePayload`, and the `cards` handle on the bot. A card is one `interactive` message whose content is replaced by `PATCH /im/v1/messages/{id}`, so the mode declares `patch: never`, `partKindOf` answers `card-inline` for every card, and `CARD_STREAM_INTERVAL` survives as the edit cadence (200 ms against the platform's 5 QPS per message); `cardStreaming: false` now only selects the buffered `final` strategy. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-lark/tests/{bot,card,send,stream}.spec.ts`. The `api/client.ts` module doc no longer points at that route map. The `config.ts` descriptions follow that behaviour: `cardStreaming` says "edit the card message in place while states stream" (with `false` buffering the states into one final `PATCH`, and a stream falling back to `post`), and `allowAtAll` says the `all` variant is declared unless it is explicitly `false`, which renders `@所有人` as text. Both also dropped the capability-probe wording of the deleted fact layer.

- **V66 · `plugin-im-adapter-lark` serves a forward's pictures through its container and expands a forward of a forward**: two facts measured against live messages, both of which V64 got wrong. First, `/messages/{id}/resources/{key}` answers `234003 File not in msg` for an entry's own id and `200` for the same key through the container the read was made for — so V64's per-entry `satori:` URL pointed at a resource nothing serves; `forwardNode` now addresses every entry by the container, which is also what makes `im_read_image` of a picture inside a forward work. Second, a forward of a forward comes back in the same answer as the whole tree — the inner container, then its entries — with every message naming its parent in `upper_message_id` and an entry appearing once per place it sits; V64 emitted only the direct children and turned the inner container into a bare `[forward]` with no identity. `forwardNode` now walks the answer in the platform's own order, tracks each entry's depth from the instance of its parent that precedes it, renders a nested container as a `[合并转发 #id]` line and indents its entries under it (capped by `FORWARD_INDENT_LIMIT`). Measured on a three-level forward of 18 items. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-lark/tests/decode.spec.ts`.
- **V67 · `plugin-im-adapter-lark` serializes card text with the mdast writer**: `card-markdown.ts` escaped literal text with a hand-written character loop and rebuilt code spans and fences itself. `escapeCardText`, `cardCodeSpan` and `cardFence` now go through `mdast-util-to-markdown` (with `mdast-util-gfm`), so metacharacters, line-start block markers, code-span delimiter length and fence length follow CommonMark instead of an owned table, and a `<` that cannot open a tag stays literal. The `<` and entity-looking `&` of text keep the entity forms the platform documents (`&#60;`, `&#38;`), and `normalizeCardMarkdown` no longer escapes `<` at all: the platform decodes no entity inside a code span, so the old final pass reached the reader as `&#60;` for text such as `` `cat <name>` ``. Both packages were already transitive dependencies of the tree. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-lark/tests/card.spec.ts`.
- **V68 · `<markdown>` is a plugin element, and an `append` stream publishes only settled blocks**: `normalize()` expanded `<markdown>` before mode resolution, so the conversion never knew what it was rendering for. An `append` stream (QQ C2C `stream_messages`) keeps every character it was sent, while a growing document re-parses as it grows — `**ab` is literal text the QQ mode escapes to `\*\*ab`, `**abc**` is bold, an open fence is closed by the renderer, a paragraph becomes a table or a setext heading — so the next state no longer extended the published prefix, intermediate publication stopped, and QQ's refused recall left a half message with the answer resent below it (V58). `satori-element` no longer parses markdown: `normalize` keeps `<markdown content>` as one element (text children joined into `content`), `toText` projects its source, and the parser closure (`mdast-util-from-markdown`, `mdast-util-gfm`, `micromark-extension-gfm`) moved to the new `plugin-im-markdown`, whose `convert.ts` holds the unchanged mapping. That plugin is an ordinary Cordis plugin, not a service: `apply` registers a handler for the `markdown` tag on `Satori.elements` (`ElementContributions`, installed through `ctx.effect`, so unloading withdraws it), and exports `markdown(content)` for building the element. `plugin-im-core` names no markdown: the render engine takes handlers from the mode registry first and from the contributions second (`RenderBase.contributions`, `HandlerLookup`), so a contributed tag renders like a registered one in every mode — a mode that registers the tag itself keeps its own handler — and without the plugin the core fallback publishes the source as literal text. `RenderContext` gained `transform(content)`, which renders content in place of the current element without a degradation entry, and `stream` (`{ strategy, final }` of the state being rendered, `StreamPhase`); `StreamHost.render` takes `final` and `Bot.stream` passes the phase down, skipping an intermediate state whose body renders no node instead of opening the stream empty. The plugin renders only `settledMarkdown` (the source before the last top-level block) for the `<markdown>` that ends the message in an intermediate `append` state; final states and `patch` / `edit` streams render the whole source. The Lark adapter imports `fromMarkdown` from the new package for inbound `md` nodes; a markdown block's stable id now includes the `<markdown>` element's path (`message/markdown[0]>/…`), which changes card `element_id`s. `dsh-im-bundle` mounts the plugin as `im-markdown`. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-markdown/tests/{convert,element}.spec.ts`, the QQ adapter's `tests/stream.spec.ts` and the corpus goldens.
- **V69 · A card callback answers with the listener's toast**: `ButtonEvent` (`satori-element/src/vocabulary.ts`) gained the optional `respond(answer: ButtonAnswer)`, where `ButtonAnswer` is `{ toast?: { type: 'info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error'; content } }`. `plugin-im-adapter-lark/src/ws.ts` no longer answers `card.action.trigger` with `{}` before intake: `answerCardAction` decodes the click, attaches `respond` to `session.button` and runs intake, and answers the frame exactly once — with `{ toast }` when a listener calls `respond`, else `{}` when intake settles or `callbackAnswerMs` (new config field, default 1500 ms, at most 2500 ms; the platform drops an answer after 3 s) elapses from arrival, whichever comes first. `respond` resolves after the answer frame was written, because the platform may revert a card update made before the callback was answered; a second call, or a call after the deadline, sends nothing. A failed intake still answers `{}` and is logged as before. The QQ adapter sets no `respond`. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-lark/tests/ws.spec.ts`. A listener that answers only after asynchronous work calls `ButtonEvent.defer()` during intake, so the frame is not answered `{}` as soon as intake settles; the deadline still bounds it.
- **V70 · Button presentation attributes in `satori-element` and the Lark card mode**: every `button` type takes the optional `ButtonStyle` attributes — `size` (`tiny | small | medium | large`), `width` (`default | fill | <px number>`), `icon` (a platform icon token), `confirm` (`{ title, text }`), `tip`, `disabledTip` and `variant` (the exact Lark button type: `default | primary | danger | text | primary_text | danger_text | primary_filled | danger_filled | laser`) — and `button-group` takes `width` (`auto | fill`) and `align` (`left | center | right`). `normalize` rejects a value outside those sets, a non-positive width, an empty icon or tip and an incomplete `confirm`, as it does for the required attributes. The card mode serializes them as the Lark button fields `size`, `width` (`<n>px` for a number), `icon: { tag: 'standard_icon', token }`, `hover_tips`, `disabled_tips` and `confirm` (plain-text title and text); `variant` takes precedence over the unchanged `theme` → `type` map. A `button-group` with `width="fill"` gives every column `width: 'weighted', weight: 1` and its buttons a default `width: 'fill'`, and `align` becomes the `column_set` `horizontal_align`; without attributes both serialize as before. The core fallback keeps the new attributes when it lowers `button.theme`, and other modes ignore them. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-lark/tests/card.spec.ts`, `vendor/satori-element/tests/normalize.spec.ts` and `vendor/plugin-im-core/tests/fallback.spec.ts`. A button whose label is blank (whitespace only, or no children) renders an ideographic space instead of its action id, which is an internal routing key.
- **V71 · `Bot.handleOf` in `plugin-im-core`**: a public method rebuilds a one-part `MessageHandle` from a `MessageRef` and the mode the message was published in, so a message this bot published in an earlier process can be edited (or deleted) after a restart. It validates the mode id and claims no content. Consumer: the toC deployment's interactive cards, which edit a card message on a click that arrives after a restart.
- **V72 · Hard limits checked on every send; unknown Lark codes keep the platform text**: `Bot` runs `mode.check()` on each draft of a plain `send` / `edit` (streams already did) and refuses a violating draft before any request with `PlatformError('limit', …, { published: 'no' })`, so a card over 200 elements or 30 KB is never sent. The Lark `classify` keeps the platform's own message (and the code) for a code its table does not know, instead of the generic "the platform rejected the request" (230099 carries "element exceeds the limit" only in its text).

- **V73 · Form controls in `satori-element` and `plugin-im-core`**: `<form>`, `<input>`, `<select>` and `<option>` are T1 tags (category `control`; content models `flow`, `empty`, `options`, `phrasing`; required `form.name`, `input.name`, `option.value`, while a `select` names a channel — an `id` that reports its pick, a `name` that feeds its form, or both), with the variants `input.checkbox` (a platform's own checkbox component), `select.multiple` (a multi-value picker) and `button.submit` (`<button type="submit">`, which submits the `<form>` it stands in — the QQ keyboard's label fallback covers every button type, so a `submit` one renders like an action). `normalize` validates each control's mode, bounds and value type and keeps `select` children to `option`; `toText` projects a form as the labels and options a reader would have used (`[Title]`, `☑ I agree`, `[选择: A / B]`); the core fallback table lowers `form` to its children, `input`/`select` to that text while reporting `interaction-dropped`, and strips `button.submit` to `button[type=action]`, so the click survives and only the submitted values are lost. A `<select>` with an `id` reports its pick through `onSelect`: the new `SelectEvent` (id, values, data, referrer, time, `respond`/`defer`) and the new `interaction/select` event, routed by `CallbackRegistry.registerSelect` / `dispatchSelect` (buttons and selects are separate keyspaces, so one id may carry both); a select without one is a form field only, and the engine collects no callback for it. A submit click stays a `ButtonEvent`, whose new optional `values` carries the form's controls keyed by `name`. `TransformResult.actions` became a `kind`-tagged `InteractionAction` union so the send stage registers an `onSelect` like an `onClick`, and `select` joined the engine's structural-container rule (`option` children). Covered by `vendor/satori-element/tests/{normalize,text,variants}.spec.ts` and `vendor/plugin-im-core/tests/{registry,fallback,session,bot,stream,testing}.spec.ts`.
- **V74 · `plugin-im-adapter-lark` renders form controls and routes their interactions**: the card mode encodes `<form>` as the platform `form` container, `<input>` as `input` (`multiline`/`password` through `input_type`) or `checker` for `type="checkbox"`, `<select>` as `select_static` / `multi_select_static` with `options` and `initial_option` / `selected_values` (from `value`, or from an `<option selected>` when the select declares none), and `<button type="submit">` as a button with `form_action_type: 'submit'`. A select carries the `{ v4: { id, data } }` callback behavior unless `callbacks: false` — it still renders and still feeds its form, it just sends no event of its own; a `multiple` select carries it too (the platform treats every interactive component as reporting its own click), and inside a form the settled value also rides in the submit's `action.form_value[<name>]`. An `<input>` gets a behavior only for `type="checkbox"`, where `checker` is the one form control that reports every toggle (`action.tag: 'checker'`, `action.checked`); a text field has none and reaches the code only through the submit's `form_value`. A control with neither an enclosing `<form>` nor a callback of its own is reported `dropped`, because nothing about it can come back. `cardActionSession` decodes `action.tag`: `select_static` (and a `multi_select_static` tag, which another card builder may still emit) becomes an `interaction/select` session with `option` / `options` as `values`, `checker` becomes an `interaction/check` session with `checked`, any other action keeps producing `interaction/button`, and `action.form_value` is decoded into `ButtonEvent.values` (strings, booleans and string arrays; numbers as strings). `@deepseek-ai/dsh-im` re-emits the new interaction as `im/select` under the same admission rule as a click. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-lark/tests/{card,ws}.spec.ts`, the refreshed card/post goldens, and `packages/experimental/im/tests/outputs.spec.ts`.
- **V75 · `interaction/check` routes a checkbox toggle (`satori-element`, `plugin-im-core`, `plugin-im-adapter-lark`, `dsh-im`)**: `input` gained `id` and `onChange` (`CheckEvent`: id, checked, data, referrer, time, `respond`/`defer`) and lost its required `name` — a control names its channel with `name` (form key), `id` (toggle callback) or both, and `normalize` rejects `onChange` on anything but `type="checkbox"` (the element table no longer lists `name` as a required `input` attribute — the alternative channel is checked there instead). `CallbackRegistry` gained a third keyspace (`registerCheck` / `getCheck` / `dispatchCheck`, so one id may carry a click, a pick and a toggle), `InteractionAction` a `'check'` kind, and `SessionEvent.check` / `Session.check` the event the bot routes. The card mode gives a checkbox with an id the `{ v4: { id } }` behavior: the platform's 勾选器回调示例 reports `action.tag: 'checker'` and `action.checked` on every toggle, unlike a text input. `cardActionSession` decodes `checker` into `interaction/check`, `dsh-im` re-emits it as `im/check` (`ImCheckEvent`), and `plugin/im-card` mints a token for `<input type="checkbox" onChange>` and answers `im/check`. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-core/tests/session.spec.ts`, `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-lark/tests/{card,ws}.spec.ts`, `packages/experimental/im/tests/outputs.spec.ts` and `plugin/im-card/test/{service,runtime}.test.ts`.

- **V76 · `plugin-im-core` bounds a resource fetch by bytes**: `createResourceFetcher(ctx, policy)` takes an optional `ResourceFetchPolicy` with `maxBytes` and refuses an over-limit resource with the new `ResourceTooLargeError` — from the declared `content-length` first, then chunk by chunk while the body is read, so the bytes past the limit are never buffered. Without a policy the fetcher reads the body in one call, exactly as upstream. Rationale: the inbound media of a message is downloaded on behalf of whoever wrote that message, and `dsh-im`'s `media.admitAs` compared the size only after `arrayBuffer()` had the whole body in memory, so one chat member decided how much this process allocates. `dsh-im` passes `media.maxBytes` into the fetch and reports the refusal as the same `too-large` outcome it already had. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-core/tests/resource.spec.ts` and `packages/experimental/im/tests/media.spec.ts`.
- **V77 · `plugin-im-adapter-lark` and `plugin-im-adapter-qq` leave a cancelled publication unknown**: `classify` keeps the cancellation `fatal` — a cancel is never retried — but reports `published: 'unknown'` instead of `'no'`, honouring a `published` the thrown error itself carries. Rationale: a `fetch` rejected with `AbortError` covers both "the request never left" and "the platform answered and the response body was cancelled", and the file-destined verdict `'no'` made `dsh-im` report `failed`, whose guidance lets the model send the same content again — a duplicate when the first one was published. The pre-request cancellation in each adapter's `api/token.ts` still reports `'no'`, because no request exists there. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-lark/tests/errors.spec.ts` and `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-qq/tests/errors.spec.ts`.
- **V78 · `plugin-im-core` reports a prepare-stage failure as unpublished**: `Bot.send` runs the pipeline (normalize → transform → prepare → serialize) inside `unpublished()`, which classifies a pipeline failure and marks it `published: 'no'`, passing an already classified refusal through and keeping `StrictRenderError` (and `PartialSendError`, which cannot arise there) unchanged. Rationale: only `publish` called `classifyError`, so a failed resource fetch or upload — where no platform message can exist — reached `dsh-im` as an unknown outcome. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-core/tests/bot.spec.ts`.
- **V79 · `plugin-im-core` does not cache a `file:` resource across publications**: `prepare` keeps a platform key only for a source that is not a `file:` URL (`isMutableSource`), while still deduplicating one upload per source within a single `prepare()` call. Rationale: the cache key is `sha256(src)`, `file:` names local bytes that change without their URL changing, and a platform key usually has no expiry, so a second publication of an edited path re-sent the earlier bytes. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-core/tests/bot.spec.ts`.
- **V80 · `plugin-im-markdown` carries the whole element vocabulary from markdown**: `convert.ts` runs mdast → hast (`mdast-util-to-hast`, raw HTML kept) → `hast-util-raw` (parse5: it pairs tags, decodes entities and tolerates sloppy HTML) → Satori elements, and the last step is driven by the vocabulary — `resolveTag` asks `tagAliases`/`isTag`, `elementInfo` decides the content model and the required attributes, so `**x**`, `<strong>x</strong>`, `<u>x</u>`, `<spoiler>x</spoiler>`, `<at user_id="ou_x">张三</at>`, `<span color="red">x</span>`, `<details>` and every other registered element take one path. Only the content categories (inline, block, media) are authorable: an interactive control (`button`, `input`, `select`, `form`), a renderer directive (`fallback`, `case`) or an inbound wrapper (`raw`, `forward`) keeps its children as text, so markdown cannot hand a reader a control the sender never sent. Two mdast rewrites run before the HTML stage: a self-closing tag whose element holds no children (`<at id=ou_x />`) is closed explicitly, because HTML reads the slash as nothing and nests the rest of the line inside that element, and footnote markers/definitions become the literal `[^label]` plus their blocks instead of GFM's `<sup>` reference and end-of-document list. Placement follows the vocabulary too: a block element on a line of its own becomes that block (`<small>…</small>`, via `soleBlock`), while the same element inside a sentence keeps its text, because `normalize` refuses a whole message for one block standing in phrasing content, and a list item outside its list degrades the same way. `package.json` adds `mdast-util-to-hast`, `hast-util-raw` pinned `~9.1.1` (9.2.0 declares `parse5@^8` and calls the tokenizer's removed `flushCharacters`, so it throws) and `@types/hast`. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-markdown/tests/convert.spec.ts`.
- **V81 · `plugin-im-core` and `plugin-im-adapter-lark` read a chat's members**: `protocol.ts` gains `MembersPage`, `Bot` gains the optional `members?(chat, cursor?, limit?)` read hook beside `getMessage`/`getMessageList` (an adapter without it leaves the operation `unavailable`), and the Lark adapter answers it from `GET /im/v1/chats/{chat_id}/members` (`api/client.ts#getChatMembers`, `open_id` addressing, page size capped at the platform's 100, a member reported without an id skipped because nothing can address it). Rationale: a mention addresses a platform user id, and a model that saw only names had no way to obtain one. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-lark/tests/bot.spec.ts`.
- **V82 · `plugin-im-adapter-lark` writes link labels with entities instead of backslashes**: `card-markdown.ts#linkLabel` escapes the characters that end a label or open a tag (`& < > [ ] \` `` ` `` `* _ ~`) as the numeric entities the platform decodes in markdown text, and `textMarkdown` uses it for a bare URL and for text inside a link label. Rationale: the GFM text serializer escapes the `:` of URL-shaped text so plain text cannot become an autolink, but a card shows that backslash to the reader (`autolink https\://example.com/b`, 2026-11-11, a real card), and a label is never autolinked. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-lark/tests/card.spec.ts`.
- **V83 · `plugin-im-core` lets the caller pin a fetch to the admitted URL and bound it**: `ResourceFetchPolicy` gains `redirect` (`RequestInit.redirect`, forwarded to `ctx.http.get`) and `timeout`, a deadline of the whole fetch, body included: the fetcher joins `AbortSignal.timeout(timeout)` with the caller's signal, hands it to `ctx.http.get` and races every body read against it, and rejects with the new `ResourceTimeoutError` when it passes. The transport's own `timeout` is not used for it, because `ctx.http` clears that timer as soon as the response headers arrive. `dsh-im` passes `redirect: 'error'` and `media.timeoutMs` for inbound media. Rationale: `dsh-im` admitted a source by classifying the address its host resolves to, then the fetch followed a 302 to `127.0.0.1` or `169.254.169.254`, so a chat member's picture reached an address the policy had refused; and nothing bounded the download at all, so a slowly trickled body held the chat's arrival order open. The `satori:` hook answers its own 3xx and ignores `redirect`, so internal platform resources are unaffected. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-core/tests/resource.spec.ts` and `packages/experimental/im/tests/media.spec.ts`.
- **V84 · `plugin-im-core` reports the result of one publication on `send`**: the event is declared `'send'(bot: Bot, result: SendResult)` and emitted as `ctx.emit('send', this, result)`; upstream (pin `662c3daf`, `packages/core/src/index.ts:64`) declares `'send'(session: Session)` and emits the adapter session. Rationale: `dsh-im` stores the bot's own publication — the platform message ids, the content tree and the chat it went to — and a `Session` carries no `MessageHandle`. Consumers depend on the vendored signature: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-im` listens `ctx.on('send', (bot, result) => …)`, reads `result.handle.parts[0]` and `result.handle.target`, and derives the own message's `message`/`seq` from them, so a sync that restores the upstream signature silently breaks own-message storage and every receipt that names a message. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-core/tests/bot.spec.ts` and `packages/experimental/im/tests/intake.spec.ts`.
- **V85 · `plugin-im-markdown` keeps the breaks beside inline formatting, resolves only own aliases and reads the everyone id**: `convert.ts#pushText` keeps a newline at either end of a text run as a `<br>` unless `trimLineEdges` finds a neighbour that already ends the line (a `<br>`, a block element, the container edge); `resolveTag` accepts an alias only when `Object.hasOwn(tagAliases, name)`; `attrsOf` turns an `at` of type `user` whose id is `all` or `here` into that mention type. Rationale: `first\n**second**\nthird` became `firstsecondthird` because the split's empty pieces were filtered with the breaks they stood for; `<constructor>` resolved to the inherited `Object` and threw in `isContent`, so an inbound post holding it could not be decoded or acknowledged; and `<at user_id="all">` reached the modes as a `user` mention, past the `all` variant `allowAtAll: false` withholds. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-markdown/tests/convert.spec.ts`.
- **V86 · `plugin-im-adapter-lark` never mentions everyone for a `user` mention and sanitizes `mention.id` in post mode**: `shared.ts#mentionMarkdown` (post) and `card-markdown.ts#cardMention` (card) strip characters outside `[\w-]` from `mention.id` before checking `isEveryoneId`, and render a `user` mention whose id is `all` or `here` as its literal `@name` label. Rationale: Feishu reads `user_id="all"` / `<at id=all>` as @everyone, and a mode decides whether a mention is allowed from its `type`, so `allowAtAll: false`, which withholds only the `all` variant, let a `user` mention carrying that id reach the platform as @everyone; post mode also interpolated raw `mention.id` into `<at user_id="…">`, so a non-identifier character such as `"` broke the tag attribute or bypassed `isEveryoneId` (`all"`). `plugin-im-markdown` now also reads `<at user_id="all">` as the `all` mention. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-lark/tests/post.spec.ts`, `card.spec.ts` and `vendor/plugin-im-markdown/tests/convert.spec.ts`.
- **V87 · `plugin-im-adapter-lark` streams internal `satori:` resource routes instead of buffering `arrayBuffer()`**: `api/client.ts` adds `downloadStream`, `getResourceStream` and `getImageStream` (returning the upstream `Response` after status validation without reading its body), and `bot.ts`'s `/messages/:messageId/resources/:fileKey` and `/images/:imageKey` internal routes return those responses directly. Rationale: `getResource` and `getImage` called `response.arrayBuffer()` and rebuilt a fresh `Response` with only `content-type`, so `createResourceFetcher`'s `maxBytes` check (V76) neither saw `content-length` nor cancelled the stream before the whole upstream file had already been buffered in process memory. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-lark/tests/bot.spec.ts`.
- **V88 · `plugin-im-core` forwards `init.signal` across `satori:` internal routes and 3xx redirects**: `Satori`'s `http/fetch` hook passes `init.signal` into the `Request` handed to `handleInternalRoute`, races `handleInternalRoute` against `init.signal` (cancelling any late response body), and preserves `signal` when following an internal 3xx `location`. Rationale: without `signal` on the internal `Request`, a resource route such as Lark's `/messages/:messageId/resources/:fileKey` saw an inert `request.signal`, so `createResourceFetcher`'s `timeout` (V83) or caller cancellation never aborted a stalled upstream fetch before headers arrived. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-core/tests/resource.spec.ts` and `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-lark/tests/bot.spec.ts`.
- **V89 · `plugin-im-adapter-lark` and `plugin-im-adapter-qq` observe mid-flight caller cancellation in `AccessToken.get`**: `AccessToken.get(signal)` races the shared `refresh()` promise against `signal` (cleaning up the abort listener on settle) and rejects the cancelled caller with `PlatformError('fatal', …, { published: 'no' })` without aborting the shared token refresh for concurrent callers. Rationale: `get(signal)` previously checked `signal?.aborted` only on entry, so `send.operationTimeoutMs` or caller cancellation waited out a hung token endpoint, and throwing a raw `AbortError` from `signal.reason` would lose the pre-request `published: 'no'` guarantee (V77). Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-lark/tests/bot.spec.ts` and `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-qq/tests/token.spec.ts`.
- **V90 · `plugin-im-adapter-lark` resolves explicit `Target.thread` ids to a reply anchor instead of falling back to chat-level `createMessage`**: `replyPlan` and `sendMessagePayload` validate non-empty chat-scoped `Target.thread` strings, reuse a matching `LarkReferrer` (`threadId`, `rootId`, or `messageId` in the same chat) or `ctx.previous[0]`'s thread root when available, and otherwise resolve `om_…` roots via `GET /im/v1/messages/{id}` or `omt_…` threads via `GET /im/v1/messages?container_id_type=thread&sort_type=ByCreateTimeAsc&page_size=1` (verifying `chat_id` and classifying pre-send read failures with `published: 'no'`) before posting to `POST /im/v1/messages/{anchor}/reply` with `reply_in_thread: true`. Rationale: Feishu's `createMessage` has no `thread_id` parameter, so `Target.thread: 'omt_…'` without a matching referrer previously created an unthreaded chat message or replied to an unrelated referrer's thread. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-lark/tests/send.spec.ts` and `packages/experimental/im/tests/send.spec.ts`.
- **V91 · Satori PR #416 protocol placement and ecosystem metadata**: the protocol module is part of `plugin-im-core` (`src/protocol.ts`), not a package of its own, with independently pinned `element`, `http`, and `fetch-file` dependencies; the package set itself is V31's. Local source imports and type-only specifiers follow V4 and V17. The core ecosystem metadata uses `im` and `@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-im-*`; runtime service names, events, and `satori:` URLs retain their upstream names. README code examples use the scoped imports. Package READMEs are copied only where upstream supplies a package README; root Satori documentation is not duplicated into packages. Element comes from its independent repository: npm 0.3.0 metadata still points to an older WebUI commit with an incompatible export API.
- **V92 · Core rc.12 compatibility in `plugin-im-core`**: `plugin-im-core/src/session.ts` reads `bot.ctx[Context.root]` instead of `bot.ctx.root`. `http/` needs no such adaptation: its source comes from the `v4.0.0-rc.13` tag, whose `packages/http` imports only `Context` and `Service` from Core and resolves intercepts through `[Service.resolveIntercept]()`, which rc.12 already provides, so the package's `cordis ^4.0.0-rc.13` peer range is not carried over. `http/README.md` keeps the documentation of the former `cordiverse/http` repository, because the rc.13 package README is a title only. That resolution is upstream's: `config`, the context intercept and the request config are merged shallowly, so a `headers` object at a later level replaces an earlier one instead of merging into it. Covered by `scripts/vendor-http.spec.ts`. Retire this entry when `plugin-im-core` synchronizes against Core rc.12.
- **V93 · `plugin-im-core` retries unknown-outcome sends only when the adapter guarantees idempotency**: `Adapter.idempotentSend?(target, ctx)` lets an adapter report whether `sendPayload` carries platform deduplication (`LarkBot` checks `options.idempotencyKey`, `QQBot` checks `options.idempotencyKey` plus an active passive ticket via `PassiveManager.canClaim`); `Bot.withRetry` retries `retryable` / `rate-limit` errors only when `classified.published === 'no'` or `idempotent` is `true`, so an un-deduplicated QQ active send never duplicates on a lost response. Also in `plugin-im-adapter-lark/src/send.ts`, `replyPlan` falls through to `resolveReplyMessageId` when a quoted message's stored referrer lacks thread metadata instead of rejecting before platform verification. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-core/tests/bot.spec.ts`, `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-qq/tests/send.spec.ts`, and `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-lark/tests/send.spec.ts`.
- **V94 · `plugin-im-core` observes pending body reads when `abortable` sees an already-aborted signal**: `resource.ts#abortable` attaches `void pending.catch(() => {})` before returning `Promise.reject(signal.reason)` when `signal.aborted` is already true, so an in-flight `reader.read()` or `response.arrayBuffer()` rejected by the abort cannot escape as an `unhandledRejection` (which triggers `app-boot` fail-loud exit). Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-core/tests/resource.spec.ts`.
- **V95 · `plugin-im-core` forwards the scheduler lifecycle signal in `StreamTickContext.options`**: `Scheduler.context` merges `{ ...this.options, signal }` into `options` so `createEditDriver.open` (which passes `ctx.options` to `adapter.sendPayload`) receives the scheduler's `AbortSignal` and `stream.abort()` / `dispose()` cancels an in-flight initial publish. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-core/tests/stream.spec.ts`.
- **V96 · `plugin-im-core` guards `Scheduler.retry` on initial `open` with `published === 'no' || idempotentSend`**: `StreamHost.idempotentSend?(ctx)` delegates to `Adapter.idempotentSend`, and `Scheduler.retry` skips retrying `published !== 'no'` on `driver.open` unless `idempotentSend` returns `true` (re-checking after backoff sleep, preserving any earlier `published: 'unknown'` across retries including `StreamLimitError`, documenting both in `Scheduler.retry`'s JSDoc, and preventing `tick()` from falling back to `host.send()` when an earlier open attempt was `published: 'unknown'`). Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-core/tests/stream.spec.ts`.
- **V97 · `plugin-im-core` accumulates `published: 'unknown'` across `Bot.withRetry` attempts**: if any retry attempt throws `published: 'unknown'`, `Bot.withRetry` preserves `published: 'unknown'` on the final thrown `PlatformError` even if a subsequent attempt fails with `published: 'no'`, so callers never treat an uncertain send as definitely unpublished. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-core/tests/bot.spec.ts`.
- **V98 · `plugin-im-core` includes `ResourceMeta` in `resourceCacheKey`**: `resourceCacheKey` and `prepare()` include `meta.name`, `meta.mime`, `meta.duration`, `meta.width`, and `meta.height` in the cache and in-flight deduplication key, so identical-byte `data:` URLs with different filenames or metadata do not reuse another file's platform `file_key`. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-core/tests/resource.spec.ts`.
