- **V99 · `plugin-im-core` clears `Scheduler._handle` after a confirmed recall and records `StreamAbortError.recalled`**: `Scheduler.recall` clears `this._handle` to `undefined` when `host.recall` returns `true` (and `MessageStream.handle` documents this lifecycle, while `StreamLimitError.handle` keeps the recalled handle for diagnostics), and `StreamAbortError` carries `recalled: boolean` so `ImSender` distinguishes a recalled stream (`failed`) from one whose message remains in the chat (`partial`). Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-core/tests/stream.spec.ts` and `packages/experimental/im/tests/send.spec.ts`.
- **V100 · `plugin-im-core` and `plugin-im-adapter-lark` report platform `thread` and `referrer` on `SentPart`**: `SentPart` gains optional `thread` and `referrer` fields, and Lark's `sendMessagePayload` populates them from `answer.thread_id`, `answer.root_id`, `target.chat.type`, and the sent `message_id` so `dsh-im` persists newly created threads and their reply context on own messages. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-lark/tests/send.spec.ts` and `packages/experimental/im/tests/intake.spec.ts`.
- **V101 · `plugin-im-adapter-qq` keeps its gateway `close` listener across `WsClientBase` abort**: `QQWsClient.accept` detaches `close` inside the `close` handler itself rather than inside `cleanup`, so non-resumable close codes (4006/4007) still run `dropSession()` after `WsClientBase`'s earlier `close` handler aborts `connection.signal`. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-qq/tests/ws.spec.ts`.
- **V102 · `plugin-im-adapter-qq` advances the resume `seq` cursor only after `bot.receive` persists**: `QQWsClient` advances `this.seq` only after `dispatch()` completes without error; if `bot.receive()` rejects it aborts the per-connection `AbortController` synchronously (preventing already-queued frames from advancing `this.seq` before the async `close` event) and closes the socket (`3000`) so `WsClientBase` reconnects and `RESUME`s from the last persisted sequence number (while decode failures still log and keep the socket up). Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-qq/tests/ws.spec.ts`.
- **V103 · `plugin-im-core` invalidates `createEditDriver`'s published cache when `editPayload` fails**: `createEditDriver`'s `edit()` helper deletes `handle` from `published` in its `catch` block so a subsequent `close()` with the earlier payload still writes back to the platform instead of skipping on a stale cache hit. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-core/tests/stream.spec.ts`.
- **V104 · `plugin-im-core`, `plugin-im-adapter-lark`, and `plugin-im-adapter-qq` use valid WHATWG client `WebSocket.close()` codes**: client-initiated abnormal closes (`WsClientBase`, `LarkWsClient`, `QQWsClient`) pass `3000` instead of `1011` or `1008`, because `undici.WebSocket` throws `InvalidAccessError` for client close codes outside `1000` and `3000–4999`. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-qq/tests/ws.spec.ts` and `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-lark/tests/ws.spec.ts`.
- **V105 · `plugin-im-adapter-qq` and `plugin-im-adapter-lark` mark all token-acquisition failures as `published: 'no'`**: `AccessToken.refresh()` and `cancelledTokenError()` in both adapters (plus QQ's `bot.ts` token poster status check) ensure transport errors, HTTP 4xx/429/5xx responses (preserving `kind`, `retryAfterMs`, `cause`, and `body`), empty token responses, and rethrown `PlatformError` / `LarkApiError` failures carry `published: 'no'` so callers can safely retry with platform backoff or record `failed` rather than `uncertain`. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-qq/tests/token.spec.ts` and `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-lark/tests/bot.spec.ts`.
- **V106 · `plugin-im-core` re-evaluates `idempotentSend` across `Bot.withRetry` attempts**: `Bot.send` passes `() => this.adapterHooks.idempotentSend?.(target, ctx) ?? false` into `Bot.withRetry` (whose unused `target` parameter is removed), and `withRetry` checks it both before and after backoff sleep (requiring `isIdempotent()` once any prior attempt returned `published: 'unknown'`, even if a later attempt returned `published: 'no'`) so an expiring time-bounded deduplication window aborts the retry as `published: 'unknown'`. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-core/tests/bot.spec.ts`.
- **V107 · `plugin-im-adapter-qq` exempts live ticketed windows from passive LRU eviction**: `PassiveManager.shrink()` only evicts entries with `tickets.size === 0` when enforcing `max` (and `PassiveManagerOptions.max` / `DEFAULT_MAX_WINDOWS` document this soft bound) so an in-flight retry's `(msg_id, msg_seq)` dedupe ticket is retained until its window expires. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-qq/tests/passive.spec.ts`.
- **V108 · `plugin-im-adapter-qq` and `plugin-im-adapter-lark` match structural `ResponseLike` in `responseOf`**: `responseOf()` in both adapters' `errors.ts` checks `typeof status === 'number' && typeof headers?.get === 'function'` instead of `instanceof Response`, because `ctx.http` uses `undici.fetch` whose `Response` is not an instance of global `Response`. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-qq/tests/token.spec.ts` and `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-lark/tests/errors.spec.ts`.
- **V109 · `plugin-im-core` and `plugin-im-adapter-lark` forward `AbortSignal` through `editPayload` and bound abort-close**: `Adapter.editPayload`, `EditDriverAdapter.editPayload`, `createEditDriver` (`tick`/`close`), `Bot.applyEdit`, and Lark's `editMessagePayload` forward `signal` to `updateMessage`/`patchMessage`, and `Scheduler.abort()` bounds its best-effort `driver.close` with `AbortSignal.timeout(STREAM_ABORT_CLOSE_TIMEOUT_MS)`. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-core/tests/stream.spec.ts`.
- **V110 · `plugin-im-core` detaches the caller `AbortSignal` listener when a stream settles**: `Scheduler` keeps a reference to its `abort` listener and removes it in `close()`, `fail()`, and `abort()`, preventing settled streams from accumulating on a long-lived `AbortSignal`. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-core/tests/stream.spec.ts`.
- **V111 · `plugin-im-adapter-qq` sends heartbeat sequence numbers in `d` per the QQ gateway protocol**: `QQWsClient.heartbeat()` sends `{ op: Opcode.HEARTBEAT, d: this.seq ?? null }` instead of `{ op: Opcode.HEARTBEAT, s: this.seq }` (upstream `adapters/qq/src/ws.ts` sends `s`, contradicting its own `HEARTBEAT` payload type `d: number` and causing strict gateways to omit `HEARTBEAT_ACK`). Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-qq/tests/ws.spec.ts`.
- **V112 · `http` combines caller `config.signal` via `AbortSignal.any` instead of an unbounded listener**: `Http[Service.invoke]` fuses `config.signal` with the per-request timeout `controller.signal` using `AbortSignal.any([config.signal, controller.signal])` so repeated requests sharing a long-lived `AbortSignal` do not accumulate strong closure listeners while still supporting response-body cancellation.
- **V113 · `plugin-im-core` and `plugin-im-adapter-qq` preserve `message_scene.ext.msg_idx` as `InboundMessage.aliases`**: `InboundMessage` gains optional `aliases?: string[]`, and QQ's `messageSession()` records `message_scene.ext.msg_idx` there while keeping `payload.id` as `message.id` (for event dedupe and passive reply `msg_id`), allowing `dsh-im` to resolve `ref_msg_idx` quotes back to the stored original message. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-qq/tests/decode.spec.ts` and `packages/experimental/im/tests/intake.spec.ts`.
- **V114 · `plugin-im-adapter-lark` wraps card callback answers in `{ code: 200, data }`**: `LarkWsClient.answerCardAction()` wraps the JSON business body (`{}` or `{ toast }`) as base64 in `{ code: 200, data: Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(body)).toString('base64') }` to match the Lark WebSocket `card.action.trigger` response envelope (upstream satori's ws does not return card callback answers). Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-lark/tests/ws.spec.ts`.
- **V115 · `plugin-im-adapter-lark` marks HTTP 200 responses missing `data` as `published: 'unknown'`**: `LarkApi.answer()` passes `published: 'unknown'` on `LarkApiError` when an HTTP 200 envelope omits `data`, matching `requiredKey()` so `dsh-im` records `uncertain` instead of `failed`. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-lark/tests/send.spec.ts`.
- **V116 · `plugin-im-core` and `plugin-im-adapter-qq` preserve `ext_info.ref_idx` on `SentPart.aliases`**: `SentPart` gains optional `aliases?: string[]`, and QQ's `sendMessagePayload()` records `answer.ext_info?.ref_idx` there while keeping `answer.id` as `part.id`, so `dsh-im` can resolve quotes against the bot's own published QQ messages. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-qq/tests/send.spec.ts` and `packages/experimental/im/tests/intake.spec.ts`.
- **V117 · `plugin-im-adapter-lark` uses null-prototype lookup tables in `prepare.ts`**: `DOCUMENT_MIME`, `DOCUMENT_EXTENSION`, and `IMAGE_NAME` use `Object.create(null)` so filenames or MIME strings matching `Object.prototype` keys (`constructor`, `__proto__`) fall back to `'stream'` instead of inheriting prototype values. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-lark/tests/prepare.spec.ts`.
- **V118 · `fetch-file` aborts `fileTypeFromStream` sniffing on `init.signal`**: `fetchFile()` checks `init.signal?.aborted` before and after sniffing, races `fileTypeFromStream` against `init.signal`, destroys the underlying read stream on abort, and rethrows abort errors instead of mapping them to 500, so `Bot.send()` timeouts are not hung by blocked local files. Covered by `vendor/fetch-file/tests/node.spec.ts`.
- **V119 · `plugin-im-adapter-lark` sets a non-empty `name` on form submit buttons (and guards empty form names)**: Feishu Card JSON 2.0 rejects clicking a `form_action_type: 'submit'` button without a non-empty `name` with client error `200530` (Empty form name). `serializeButton` now emits `name: button.id` alongside `form_action_type: 'submit'` (using the card-unique `element_id` finalized by `finalize`), and `serializeComponent` falls back to `component.id` if a `form`'s `name` is empty. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-lark/tests/card.spec.ts` and the refreshed `form` / `everything` card goldens.
- **V120 · `plugin-im-core` and `plugin-im-adapter-lark` decode inbound reaction events without `chat_id` and normalize app operators**: `SessionEvent.reaction.message.chat` is optional and `Session` exposes a `reaction` getter, because Feishu's `im.message.reaction.created_v1` / `deleted_v1` payloads carry `message_id` without `chat_id`. `LarkBot`'s `reactionSessions()` emits `reaction-added` / `reaction-removed` even when `chat_id` is absent (letting `dsh-im` resolve the stored message by id) and normalizes `operator_type === 'app'` matching `bot.config.appId` to `bot.selfId` so downstream filters can skip self-reactions. Covered by `vendor/plugin-im-adapter-lark/tests/decode.spec.ts` and `packages/experimental/im/tests/outputs.spec.ts`.

### Resolver adaptations

Relative to the resolver source in Cordis `v4.0.0-rc.12`:

- **Web build imports:** `loader/src/resolve.ts` and `loader/src/config/tree.ts` use default imports for Node builtin modules to support the Web shell's browser externalization. The shell supplies its own module loader.
- **Package-scope cache keys:** `loader/src/resolve.ts` normalizes directory paths with `path.resolve()` before finding the package scope. A root config and a nested config in the same package therefore share the same cached resolver promise and helper-file write. Covered by `scripts/cordis-loader-resolve.spec.ts`.

## Sync procedure

To update a vendored package from upstream:

1. In the upstream repository listed in the manifest, check out the release tag or commit to sync and note its full commit SHA.
2. Copy the package's `src/` (and `bin.js`, `README.md`, `LICENSE` if changed) over the vendored directory.
3. Re-apply the local modifications listed above (or drop them if upstream made them unnecessary — update the log either way).
4. Update the version and commit hash in the manifest table.
5. Run `pnpm install && pnpm run test && pnpm run build` at the repo root.
